title: Frontend: Navbar
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Navbar. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({current="home"}). A Menu disclosure button controls nav#site-nav, initially hidden. Links Home and About have aria-current=page only for current. Clicking a link or Escape on the Menu button closes the nav. Use native links with local hashes.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use nav and ordinary links for page navigation.
alternativeApproaches: Handle focus restoration when a mobile drawer closes after an in-app route change.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Current route; mobile open/close; Escape.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
